knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Using the fact that

$$
165^\circ=225^\circ-60^\circ,
$$

calculate the **exact** value of $\cos\left(165^\circ\right)$.

$\cos\left(165^\circ\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x-y)=\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(165^\circ\right)=\cos\left(225^\circ-60^\circ\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(225^\circ\right)\cos\left(60^\circ\right)+\sin\left(225^\circ\right)\sin\left(60^\circ\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\right) \\
&=- \frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the **exact** value of $\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)$.

*Hint: Use the fact that*

$$
\frac{5\pi}{12}=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{6}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\
&=\frac{- \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$
